chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and others from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with the fee of the middleman (simstar); he buys for the people day after day for a specified amount; he is essentially in the status of the wage-earners.

key_terms.أَجْرِ: Fee, wage, or compensation for work
key_terms.السِّمْسَارِ: Middleman or broker who facilitates trade for a fee

ai.seo_question: Is the commission or fee of a middleman (simstar) permissible in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi legitimizes the brokerage fee (ajr) by equating the simstar’s daily, specified compensation to that of a hired worker (ujara'), thereby resolving concerns regarding uncertainty (gharar) in middleman transactions. It reflects the practical jurisprudence of the Imams, who recognized the necessity of commercial intermediaries and validated their income as lawful wages for service rather than speculative gain.
